title: The Painted Confession
premise: Vesper Kavanagh, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made him both invaluable and isolated, receives two letters the same morning: one confessing to a drowning ruled accidental fifteen years ago, and one promising a second confession if he follows the clues. The trail leads him to Saltmere, a fading coastal town where the victim, artist Lena Oduya, once painted murals that locals now refuse to discuss. Vesper discovers her final mural conceals a ledger of payments — proof that half the town took hush money from the shipping company responsible for her death. As the tide threatens to reclaim the sunken evidence and the letter-writer's identity circles closer than expected, Vesper must choose between handing the ledger to authorities who were paid to look away or exposing everyone himself. In the end he paints over nothing: he photographs every wall, mails copies to every household in Saltmere, and lets the town convict itself.
about_author: Mirabel Almeida is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent a decade investigating coastal accidents before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about towns that keep their own ledgers, and lives within sight of water she does not entirely trust.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Vesper Kavanagh opens his morning mail to find twin letters in identical handwriting: one confessing to Lena Oduya's drowning, one promising 'the rest is where she left it.' His memory flags details no stranger should know. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into compulsion — for the first time, a case wants him personally.

chapters.title: The File That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: In his office archive, Vesper pulls the original claim file and finds pages subtly altered — dates shifted, a witness struck out. His photographic memory lets him reconstruct what was removed. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: cold anger; someone inside the system edited history, and only he can prove it.

chapters.title: Saltmere
chapters.summary: Vesper arrives in the coastal town where Lena drowned. The streets are friendly; the answers are not. A landlady mentions the murals, then stops mid-sentence when her son enters. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being a stranger among people rehearsing the same silence.

chapters.title: The Drowned Gallery
chapters.summary: Vesper finds Lena's surviving murals in a derelict cannery — luminous scenes of harbor life, each containing small painted figures holding objects he doesn't yet understand. He photographs everything. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: awe curdling into suspicion; the paintings are beautiful the way traps are beautiful.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: A retired harbormaster, Corliss, tells Vesper about the night Lena went out alone, and about the shipping company, Meridian Freight, that owned the pier. He talks freely — too freely, as if scripted. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the first taste of misdirection; grief weaponized against him.

chapters.title: Second Letter
chapters.summary: A second letter waits at his boarding house: a fragment of a painted image matching the cannery murals, with coordinates written in pigment code. The writer knows exactly where Vesper has been. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: hunted intimacy — the confession writer is watching, and knows him better than strangers should.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Isn't
chapters.summary: Vesper tracks down Lena's sister, Ada Oduya, who left town years ago. She reveals Lena was documenting something before she died — and that Ada received one payment herself, which she never spent. POV: Ada (brief) then Vesper. Emotional beat: guilt inherited; belonging refused at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Pigment Ledger
chapters.summary: Working from memory and Ada's fragments, Vesper deciphers the murals' recurring objects — crates, coins, keys — as a coded record of payments: names, amounts, dates. Half of Saltmere took Meridian's money. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: vertigo; the whole town is implicated, including people who have been kind to him.

chapters.title: Kindness With Interest
chapters.summary: The landlady feeds him, warns him gently to leave, and slips a key into his coat pocket — the key painted most often in the murals. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: tenderness tangled with threat; even mercy here has a price already paid.

chapters.title: Meridian's Man
chapters.summary: A polished adjuster named Hale arrives, ostensibly on unrelated business, and offers Vesper a consulting fee to close an old file. Vesper recognizes the offer's structure from a hundred corrupt settlements. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: recognition and contempt; the machine that killed Lena is still running smoothly.

chapters.title: The Third Letter
chapters.summary: The third letter names a date — the anniversary of Lena's death — and promises the full confession 'when the tide gives up what it took.' Vesper realizes something physical is buried offshore. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: dread converting to resolve; a deadline now exists.

chapters.title: Corliss Breaks
chapters.summary: Confronted with the decoded ledger, Corliss admits he was the pier watchman who let the overloaded crane operate that night — and that he wrote the letters. But he insists he didn't kill her; he only watched. POV: Corliss. Emotional beat: shame finally spoken aloud after fifteen years of salt-water silence.

chapters.title: Who Watched the Watcher
chapters.summary: Vesper re-examines the letters' handwriting against town records and finds a second hand beneath Corliss's — someone taught him what to confess. The trail points toward the cannery's old foreman, presumed dead. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the ground shifting; the confessor himself was confessed to.

chapters.title: Ada Returns
chapters.summary: Ada arrives unannounced, having followed the same trail. Sibling-like friction between her certainty and Vesper's method becomes alliance. She reveals Lena's last unsent letter naming the foreman, Dez Calloway, as the man who helped her hide the evidence. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership; belonging offered sideways, through shared purpose.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: At extreme low tide, Vesper and Ada search the flats below the old pier and find a sealed painter's chest wedged in the pilings — Lena's originals, plus documents implicating Meridian's regional director. They are seen leaving. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: triumph immediately shadowed by exposure.

chapters.title: The Burning Cannery
chapters.summary: That night the cannery burns. Vesper runs in to photograph the remaining murals by firelight, memorizing what the flames erase, and emerges singed but with the ledger complete in his head. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: sacrifice of safety for memory; the paintings die so the record survives.

chapters.title: Hale's Patience Ends
chapters.summary: Hale detains Vesper under pretext of arson questioning, offering immunity for silence. Vesper recites the ledger's contents back to him from memory, watching the man understand that burning paper changed nothing. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: quiet power; the mind as incorruptible vault.

chapters.title: Dez Calloway
chapters.summary: The foreman, alive and hiding as a lighthouse keeper, confesses: he helped Lena hide the chest, then fled when Meridian threatened his family. He wrote the letters through Corliss because he could no longer carry it alone. POV: Dez. Emotional beat: cowardice and courage in the same breath; justice deferred, not denied.

chapters.title: Anniversary
chapters.summary: On the tide's lowest ebb, the town gathers at the shore — summoned by anonymous mailed pages Vesper sent. He lays out the evidence publicly: the ledger, the chest, the recordings. Meridian's director is present, believing his money bought the crowd. It did not. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: climax; a community choosing truth over comfort in real time.

chapters.title: What the Town Decides
chapters.summary: Saltmere turns on Meridian, not on itself: the crowd forces the director's resignation, votes to fund an independent inquiry, and refuses Hale's settlement — but also forgives those who took the money, understanding fear. Justice arrives outside the courtroom. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: catharsis; imperfect, collective, real.

chapters.title: Repainting
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Ada begins repainting the lost murals with the town's help, this time with the ledger rendered openly — names included, hers among them. Vesper watches strangers become neighbors through shared brushwork. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: belonging earned rather than found.

chapters.title: The Fifth Letter
chapters.summary: A final envelope arrives: not a confession but a thank-you, unsigned, in handwriting Vesper almost recognizes — hinting another hidden record exists elsewhere. He smiles, packs a bag, and books a ticket. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: resolution with an open door; memory, once awakened, keeps working.
